In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ultrastructural changes of liver cells in PRC are not specific for PRC but are also seen in other forms of chronic cholestasis, and that the ultrastructural morphology of orcein positive hepatocytes in chronic cholestases does not indicate the existence of a specific disease entity.
orcein positive hepatocyte material represents copper-protein complexes, which are taken into the intracellular lysosomal metabolism and are processed by the liver cells.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the orceins positive material in PBC is an intracellular metabolite, and not an intracellular precipitate.
the orceins positive material in PBC represents the intracellular copper-protein complex, which is processed by the lysosomal compartment in the liver cells.
the orceins positive material is a product of the intracellular metabolism, and that it may be related to the intracellular processing of iron compounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the orceinstaining material seen in PBC is not a specific marker for PBC, and is not a specific copper compound, but is a general marker for the presence of large particles, which are probably lysosomal structures, in liver cells.

the orceine-positive material seen in light microscopic studies of liver biopsies of PBC patients is a manifestation of an intracellular metabolic activity of the lysosomal compartment in the liver cells, and that the material resembles in many ways the iron-protein complex in the iron-storage cells of the spleen and liver.

orcein positive hepatocytes in chronic biliary diseases are the result of an activation of lysosomal metabolism, and not the result of a primary disturbance in the synthesis and secretion of copper-protein complex.
